scope: H1-H4 only. M-series already committed and untouched. This run reviewed the earlier first-pass H1-H4 working tree line by line against SPEC-02 H1-H4 and its Review checklist, kept what was correct and fixed what was wrong or missing.

kept: H1: revalidate=3600; no try/catch around getBlogPostBySlug in generateMetadata or the page; getRedirect(slug) -> permanentRedirect('/blog/' + newPath) before not-found metadata / notFound()

H2: revalidatePath (next/cache) per path, each individually try/catch-wrapped, for /blog/<slug> (old and new), /blog, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /api/blog, only after a successful create/update/delete
H3: lib/db.ts Pool connectionTimeoutMillis 10_000; middleware blog_redirects lookup raced against 5000 ms, failing open through the existing catch
H4: dynamic='force-dynamic' -> revalidate=300; try/catch removed so errors throw; success body unchanged (NextResponse.json(posts))

fixed.problem: `export const revalidate = 3600` alone had no effect: in Next 15.5 a dynamic segment with no generateStaticParams stays fully dynamic. Build listed /blog/[slug] as ƒ, prerender-manifest dynamicRoutes was empty, and at runtime every response was `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store`. So H1's ISR (and the stale-page-on-DB-error guarantee) did not exist.
fixed.fix: Added `export async function generateStaticParams() { return [] }` (dynamicParams stays default true). Prerenders nothing at build (no DB access at build for this route) and caches each slug on first request. After the fix: build shows ● /blog/[slug], dynamicRoutes contains /blog/[slug], responses are x-nextjs-cache MISS then HIT with s-maxage=3600. REVIEWER NOTE: this is the one addition beyond the literal SPEC-02 H1 text; it is what makes H1's stated behaviour (ISR) true.

fixed.problem: The pre-mutation getBlogPostById (needed only to learn the old slug for revalidation) ran unguarded inside the handler try: if it threw, the mutation was never attempted and PUT/DELETE returned 500 (PUT could also misreport it as 409 if the message contained 'unique'), i.e. revalidation plumbing could fail/alter the mutation. DELETE also skipped revalidating /blog, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /api/blog entirely when the pre-fetch returned no slug.
fixed.fix: Added a local `currentSlug(id)` helper that wraps getBlogPostById in try/catch and returns undefined on failure; PUT revalidates [oldSlug, result.slug], DELETE revalidates [oldSlug] and always the common paths. revalidateBlogPaths now takes Array<string | undefined> and drops empty entries. Status codes and bodies of every mutation path are unchanged.

fixed.problem: The 5000 ms timeout timer was never cleared, so it stayed pending after a fast lookup.
fixed.fix: Captured the timer and clearTimeout(timer) in a finally after the existing catch. Fail-open semantics unchanged.

changedFiles.change: revalidate=3600; generateStaticParams() returning []; DB errors from getBlogPostBySlug/getRedirect propagate (no try/catch) in generateMetadata and page; missing post -> getRedirect(slug) -> permanentRedirect(`/blog/${newPath}`) else not-found metadata / notFound().
Local revalidateBlogPaths helper (revalidatePath from next/cache, each call try/catch); called after a successful createBlogPost with the new slug.
Same helper plus fault-tolerant currentSlug pre-fetch; PUT revalidates old+new slug, DELETE the deleted slug, both plus the 5 common paths, only after success.
blog_redirects lookup raced with a 5000 ms rejecting timeout (cleared in finally); timeout falls into the existing fail-open catch.
new Pool({ connectionString, connectionTimeoutMillis: 10_000 }); attachDatabasePool guard under process.env.VERCEL untouched.
force-dynamic -> revalidate=300; try/catch removed so a DB error throws; success body unchanged.

findingsForReviewerAndOwner.finding: blog_redirects rows store full paths (old_path '/blog/<old>', new_path '/blog/<new>'; all 95 rows), but middleware.ts, /api/blog-redirects and SPEC-02 H1's getRedirect(slug) all look up the bare slug, so none of them ever matches. If one did match, `/blog/${newPath}` would produce '/blog//blog/<new>'. No impact today: all 95 old paths still exist as live posts, so the post renders and the redirect check is never reached. H1 was kept exactly as spec'd; the spec owner should decide whether to normalise the lookup/target.

lib/db.ts Pool has no 'error' listener: when Postgres terminated idle connections (pg_ctl stop) next start logged `uncaughtException` (57P01) twice (the process survived in this run). Consider pool.on('error', ...) in a later spec item.

Next 15.5 runs revalidatePath's pending work via waitUntil / after the response body (build/templates/app-route.js), so an async revalidation failure cannot change the mutation response; the synchronous revalidatePath throws are caught per path.
